changes.text: This Task Force replaces the classic Citadel Task Force, which has been retired to Ouroboros under Arc 0.42.
New mode now available through the Arena: Onslaught.
Custom rules are available in this mode, like other Arena match types.
This game mode is only available to be played as Timed Matches.
This game mode must be played with two teams.
These are the rules that we built the mode around to be the closest to a base PvE experience, but players are free to play however they see fit:
Time: 30 Minutes
Players: 3-8 on each team
Incarnates: Alpha Slot Only
Diminishing Returns: Disabled
Inherent Resistance: Disabled
Inspirations: Small Only
The first time Onslaught is set for an Arena event, the recommended settings are applied.
This mode is a hybrid PvPvE mode, where players will be fighting the enemy team + NPC combatants in order to progress the mode's objectives.
Like regular PvE, this mode rewards Experience, Influence, Enhancements, Recipes, and all normal drops from critters.
All enemies in this mode are level-less and ignore combat mods, but give higher (3x-5x) than normal rewards!
Played on the new Onslaught: Junction map, designed specially for this mode.
This map contains a Trainer and an Enhancement vendor located in your team's hospital, it is intended this new game mode could be utilized as an alternative leveling method!
One team plays as Longbow (The first team that zones in) and the second team plays as Arachnos.
Players spawn inside their hospital, located through a door in the back corner of their base.
Hospitals have three exit doors, allowing players to emerge from variable locations
Each team has a base core, located in their corner of the map. A team that has their base's core destroyed will lose the game!
Only your NPC lane soldiers can attack the enemy base core! You must escort your soldiers from your base to the enemy's in order to win the game.
Every 60 seconds, three eighteen-man squads of NPC lane soldiers will deploy from the bases and begin traveling towards the opponent's base.
These soldiers will stop and fight anything hostile they encounter, if nothing to engage, they will return to traveling towards the opponent's base.
Take advantage of the push/pull rhythm of the match to seize victory!
Each capture lane is lined with extremely powerful missile turrets, it will be very dangerous for players who attempt to push a lane without any back-up!
Every Defense Point has a Pillbox with four missile turrets, when all four turrets are destroyed, the Defense Point is automatically destroyed and stops providing benefits to the opposing team.
You cannot attack turrets out of order! If there are turrets in front, the turrets in back will be buffed/untouchable.
Each pillbox has a powerful forcefield on top that players can stand within like Recluse's Victory.
In order for your NPC lane soldiers to attack your opponent's base you must destroy the Defense Point on a single lane to make their core vulnerable!
This game mode has a per-match currency salvage called Onslaught Credits.
These credits are temporary salvage used only during the duration of the Onslaught match. So don't hesitate to use them as soon as you can!
Can hold 10,000 at a time.
Located under the Special Salvage tab.
Resets to zero at the beginning of an Onslaught match.
These credits can be obtained by defeating players on the enemy team! Each player's defeat is worth 250 Onslaught Credits and pays out to the one who got the killing blow!

These credits drop when defeating enemy NPC lane soldiers if you tagged them with an attack for defeat credit. This credit is team and map-wide, so be sure and deal some damage to your opponent's soldiers in order to cash in on their credits!
Soldier Minions: 5 Credits
Soldier Lieutenants: 10 Credits
Soldier Bosses: 15 Credits
Soldier Elite Bosses 20 Credits
Additionally, in-between the capture lanes in the grassy areas will spawn Rikti infiltrators every 2 minutes! These hostile Rikti are worth x2 their rank in Onslaught Credit!
Rikti Minions: 10 Credits
Rikti Lieutenants: 20 Credits
Rikti Bosses: 30 Credits
Rikti Elite Bosses: 100 Credits
NOTE: For these hostile neutral mobs, Experience, Influence, and drops are rewarded based on damage %, but the Onslaught Credits are rewarded to the team that got the killing blow!
Finally, there are special raves that will appear in the non-base corners of the map periodically (5 minutes since the last rave's AV was cleared).
These raves consist randomly of either Carnival of Shadows, Freakshow, or Trolls and their reward payout matches the Rikti for rank payouts:
Rave Lieutenants: 20 Credits
Rave Bosses: 30 Credits
Rave Elite Bosses: 100 Credits
Rave Arch-villain: Damage split 1,000 Credits + 200 for killing blow
The Rave AV's credit payout is paid out to the group that did the most damage, and rewards based on damage dealt within the last 15 seconds.
The team that got the killing blow gains an additional 200 Credits from AV defeats.
These Arch-villains have scaling HP when there are more than 8+ players present.
The Rave AV is now always randomized in sets of three. Meaning you won't get a repeat until all of them have shown up at least once.
Lane soldier mobs will ignore/not interact with jungle/rave mobs.

There are a number of ways a team can claim victory in an Onslaught match:
Knockout - Destroy your opponent's base core to win via knockout.
Timeout - At the end of the game's timer the victor will be declared based on the following criteria hierarchy:
Base Core HP%
Defense Points Defeated
Research Score
Soldier Defeats
Draw - If the game times out and all the above scores are equal, the match will result in a draw.
Forfeit - A team who has no more players will automatically forfeit the match.
At the end of the match a screen will appear that displays the match statistics to each participant:
Build to survive! We would highly recommend taking an Epic Power Pool defense/resistance power if you have one available!
If you haven't taken the Fighting Pool power, Tough, you should buy the Super Body Armor buff instead!
Be ready to move! If you aren't natively equipped to move at max speeds, pick up one of the Super Travel Powers from the Scientist shop!
Inside the hospital is a Spy NPC who will give you a preview of the match results, allowing you to survey the current state of the match!
Players can leave the match at any time with a dialog option found on the Scientist NPCs.
Don't hold onto Onslaught Credits! Have a plan on how to spend them and work towards improving you and your team's odds of victory!
Planning to focus on attacking other players? The Proc Booster upgrades will be essential in overcoming more resilient player targets!
Everyone on the team receives credits for NPC defeats, work together to push lanes and defeat Rikti to amass credits for upgrades!

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: What's the difference between Afraid, Avoid, and Morale Break? Glad you asked! This is how it is currently on Live:

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Afraid tells a mob to immediately run away to a random distant point for a minimum of 3 seconds (no matter the duration of the afraid affect, it only "checks" every so often)

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Avoid tells a mob to run to a random point just outside the Avoid circle and not to come back inside it

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Morale Break functions like Afraid, but is triggered by how the combat is going (e.g. are the mobs getting hit substantially more often than they are hitting? did the bosses in the spawn all get wiped out? etc) - Editor's note: this exists on live but doesn't have a name, we're now giving it a name for clarity in discussions

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Grief functions like Afraid, but it triggered by more extreme circumstances where the mob is low on health and has not been able to attack a player for a long time, and tells the mob to go even further than the others.

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Fixed a bug preventing Avoid effects from working (this affected Ice Storm, Rain of Fire, Sleet, Freezing Rain, Blizzard, and Rain of Arrows).

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Player versions of Caltrops and Thorntrops now apply Avoid (on live they apply Afraid).

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Monkey Gas now applies Avoid instead of Afraid.

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Reduced the distance that enemies run due to Afraid or Morale Breaks substantially. Previously they would look for a random point from 100' to 200' in any direction, now they look for a point from 30' to 100' away. If conditions persist, they may choose to run again when they reach that point. Griefed mobs will still try to run up to 300' away.

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Extra discussion about Avoid (and the fix) in the spoiler:

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: This powerset is no longer mutually exclusive with Stone Armor on Tankers and Brutes.

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Empathy now has a new overheal mechanic, where healing powers convert to Absorb shields if they heal targets that are already high on hp. The three healing powers can stack shields with each other, but not themselves. Yes, Absorb Pain is a huge Absorb shield (for absorbing lots of pain).

changes.text: Clear Mind is AoE, though the mez protection only stacks on the main target.

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Recovery Aura and Regeneration Aura now have a linger period after activation, where the Empath can run around and tag their errant teammates to give them the buff.

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Empathy has multiple powers using the same animations, resulting in buggy behavior and skipped animations. They have been subtly altered to be different. Oh, and the new ones are faster, so you can actually save your friends in an emergency before they faceplant. But in the times where you can't, well...

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
changes.text: Resurrect is now AoE! But if even that isn't enough to keep your crazy friends going...

changes.subsection: Avoid, Afraid, Morale Break, Grief changes
